messages:
sara: FYI ACME reported repeated p95 spikes and intermittent 429s on their eu3 dedicated pool since last night. Symptoms look like contention rather than model regression.

mike: Can you paste the pool id and a sample request id? Also any recent config changes?

sara: pool=ded-eu3-42, sample request id=rid_3a4f, no config changes from ACME side. They mentioned a lot of smaller parallel calls (many short sequences).

jess: Short sequences + many parallel calls => KV-cache churn + small-batch saturation is a red flag on shared nodes. Do we know MIG partitioning for that pool?

mike: Pool is a mixed-MIG setup: nodes with 1g.8gb and 2g.20gb partitions. I'll pull node mappings.

mike: quick diag logs:
```
$ rtr node-info --pool ded-eu3-42 --summary
nodes: 8
partitions: 1g.8gb(20), 2g.20gb(4)
active-tenants: 12
avg-gpu-util: 62%
kvcache-hit: 12%
rv: per-node p95 tokens: 180ms -> 420ms (spikes)
```

oliver: KV cache hit 12% is low given repeated requests. If tenant traffic pattern is many short prompts, continuous batching might underfill and cause high SM saturation. Could be noisy neighbor hogging memory bandwidth / L3.

sara: ACME says spikes correlate with tenant "brightbeam" (internal). Brightbeam runs many tiny completion calls every second.

jess: Could be lockstep KV invalidation when multiple tenants use similar prefixes. Two quick repros: 1) run curl loop with 100 concurrent short requests against pool; 2) run NVIDIA dmon on suspected node to watch mem bw / L3.

mike: Repro command we ran against a repro node:
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"model":"gpt-repro","input":"hi"}' & done; wait
```
Observed 429s after ~160 concurrent requests and p95 jump to 1.2s on that node.

oliver: Collected nvidia top/dmon during run - saw sustained SM and L3 thrash on partitioned 1g.8gb instances. Sample dmon snapshot: 
```
# gpu dmon (node-7)
mem % 94, sm % 88, l3 bw spikes 1.2GB/s
```

jess: Next actions: 1) throttle/shape brightbeam on tenant level as immediate mitigation (support policy), 2) bump autoscale threshold for pool to allow faster scale-up, 3) schedule migration of brightbeam to dedicated single-tenant node or larger partitions, 4) collect core dumps if we see OOMs.

autoscale-bot: Autoscale event: pool ded-eu3-42 attempted autoscale at 2025-10-02T02:14:02Z but suppressed due to cooldown (policy: 300s). Current replicas=8, requested=12.

mike: Looks like cooldown prevented fast-add. I'll adjust policy for this pool to 120s and allow one immediate burst replica. Doing now and will monitor.

sara: I've opened an interim customer ticket telling ACME we identified noisy neighbour candidate and will throttle brightbeam while we migrate. Also requested their permission to rotate the tenant to a dedicated node for 2 hours to confirm latency improvement.

jess: Please attach the following logs to the customer ticket: rtr-perf-sample (pre/post), dmon snapshots, and the autoscale events. If migration reduces p95 to <200ms we keep migration and plan longer-term partitioning changes.

mike: Patch applied: cooldown->120s, burst replica allowed. I'll post metrics in 10m.

oliver: For long term: recommend re-balancing pool to fewer mixed-MIG nodes and increase KV-cache size for 1g partitions, or favor larger partitions for tenants with high qps short prompts. Also add detection rule: high concurrent short sequences + kvcache-hit<20% -> mark as noisy candidate.

sara: ACME replied: "rotation helped — p95 dropped to ~180ms during the test window." They're ok with longer migration while we do partitioning plan.

mike: Closing loop: will schedule infra change and follow up with product on detection rule. Leaving thread open until partitioning plan is on calendar.

jess: Thanks team. Will add postmortem-lite to incidents if this recurs. :thumbsup:
